name: Question 3
problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{11}?$
worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{11}=-\frac{2}{3}\cdot 6=-4.$
